paper.title: A Denoising Pre-training Framework for Accelerating Novel Material Discovery
paper.research_summary: The paper introduces an unsupervised Denoising Pre-training Framework (DPF) for crystal structures to overcome the scarcity of labeled data in crystal property prediction. DPF trains models to reconstruct original crystal structures by recovering masked atom types, perturbed atom positions, and perturbed lattice constants. It pre-trains on 380,743 unlabeled crystal structures and fine-tunes on downstream property prediction tasks, demonstrating improved performance across multiple benchmarks.

stages.stage_goal: Generate perturbed crystal representations by masking atom types, adding noise to atom positions, and perturbing lattice constants.
stage_output: perturbed crystal representations (masked atom types, perturbed atom positions, perturbed lattice constants)

evidence.text: At the pre-training stage, we mask the types of crystal atoms and add noise on atom positions and lattice constants to acquire perturbed representations.
For mask language modeling, we randomly select γ of atoms in a crystal and assign a type unknown to them...
For each atom in a crystal, we randomly sample a noise η ∈R3 ∼N(0, 1) and apply it to the atom positions as follows: ˜P = {p1 + α · η1, p2 + α · η2, · · · , pn + α · ηn}
We also perturb the lattice constants with a randomly sampled Gaussian noise σ ∈R6 ∼N(0, 1) as follows: ˜L = L + β · σ

We pre-train our model on 380,743 crystal structure data filtered from the recent work (Merchant et al. 2023), excluding structures that are duplicates of downstream datasets or do not have physical or chemical significance.

The benchmark for crystal property prediction is well established. There are two standard benchmark datasets, JARVIS and Materials Project (Choudhary et al. 2020; Chen et al. 2019), to evaluate the performance of our model.
The JARVIS dataset contains 55,722 materials with critical crystal properties for functional material design, including bandgaps, formation energies, energy above hull, total energy and so on.

The benchmark for crystal property prediction is well established. There are two standard benchmark datasets, JARVIS and Materials Project (Choudhary et al. 2020; Chen et al. 2019), to evaluate the performance of our model.

The Materials Project dataset aggregates several key crystal property datasets, including formation energy, band gap, bulk moduli, and shear moduli. Among them, 69,239 crystals are labeled with properties of formation energy and band gap, while only 5,451 crystal structures are labeled with the properties of bulk moduli and shear moduli.
